newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 9.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The House ethics committee yesterday gave fugitive Representative Romeo Jalosjos until ten this morning to appear at the House or surrender to authorities. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- President Fidel Ramos approved yesterday the adoption of a national computerised identification reference system that will properly and efficiently identify Filipino citizens and foreign residents seeking basic services and social security. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- President Ramos justified yesterday his controversial decision to ban Nobel Peace Prize co-winner Jose Ramos-Horta from coming to Manila, saying the government was not consulted by those who invited the East Timorese independence crusader. (STAR/TIMES)

- Despite hefty payments of external debt, the Philippines managed to post a record $4.2-billion balance of payments surplus as of end-1996, or nearly a seven-fold increase over the end-1995 surplus of $645 million, according to preliminary data released by the Central Bank. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Department of Energy wants to implement the full deregulation of the oil indsutry ahead of March because the buffer fund for absorbing oil price increases would be depleted by February. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Department of Trade and Industry is vigorously objecting to the proposed unilateral withdrawal of refined sugar from the list of agricultural products covered by the ASEAN Free Trade Area-Common Effective Preferential Tariff scheme. (STANDARD)
- Local car assemblers increased sales last year by 24.5 percent to 88,648 units. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
